records.source: ט֤וֹב פַּ֣ת חֲ֭רֵבָה וְשַׁלְוָה־בָ֑הּ מִ֝בַּ֗יִת מָלֵ֥א זִבְחֵי־רִֽיב׃
records.gloss: Better [is] a dry morsel and quiet with it than a house full of sacrifices [with] strife.
pieces: Better a dry crust eaten in peace \q than a house full of feasting and quarrels.

L.1: Better [is] a dry crust with quiet \q than a house full of feasting with strife.

R.1: It is better to eat a little dry bread in peace \q than to have a big feast where people are fighting.

decisions.choice: sacrifices: feasting on sacrificial meat
decisions.reason: Meat from peace offerings was eaten in a family feast (7:14). A house full of it means plenty.

decisions.choice: better ... than: as in 15:16–17

records.source: עֶֽבֶד־מַשְׂכִּ֗יל יִ֭מְשֹׁל בְּבֵ֣ן מֵבִ֑ישׁ וּבְת֥וֹךְ אַ֝חִ֗ים יַחֲלֹ֥ק נַחֲלָֽה׃
records.gloss: A servant acting wisely will rule over a son acting shamefully, and among brothers he will share [the] inheritance.
pieces: A servant with good sense will end up over a son who brings disgrace, \q and will get a share of the inheritance with the brothers.

L.2: A servant who acts wisely will rule over a son who brings shame, \q and will share [the] inheritance among [the] brothers.

R.2: A wise servant may end up in charge of a son who brings shame on his family. \q The servant may even get part of the family's money.

decisions.choice: a servant sharing the inheritance: a reversal
decisions.reason: A trusted servant could be made heir when there was no worthy son (Genesis 15:2–3). Wisdom can lift a servant above a son.

records.source: מַצְרֵ֣ף לַ֭כֶּסֶף וְכ֣וּר לַזָּהָ֑ב וּבֹחֵ֖ן לִבּ֣וֹת יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: A crucible for silver and a furnace for gold, but YHWH tests hearts.
pieces: Silver is tried in the crucible and gold in the furnace, \q but it is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who tests the heart.

L.3: [The] crucible [is] for silver and [the] furnace for gold, \q but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} tests hearts.

R.3: People use fire to test silver and gold. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} tests people's hearts.

decisions.choice: crucible and furnace: refining metals
decisions.reason: Metals were heated to separate out the dross (27:21; Malachi 3:3). God tests people to show what is in them.

records.source: מֵ֭רַע מַקְשִׁ֣יב עַל־שְׂפַת־אָ֑וֶן שֶׁ֥קֶר מֵ֝זִין עַל־לְשׁ֥וֹן הַוֺּֽת׃
records.gloss: An evildoer pays attention to a lip of wickedness; deception gives ear to a tongue of destruction.
pieces: Evildoers pay attention to wicked talk; \q liars listen eagerly to malicious words.

L.4: An evildoer listens to wicked lips; \q a liar gives ear to a destructive tongue.

R.4: Evil people like to listen to evil talk. \q Liars like to listen to lies.

decisions.choice: evildoer ... liar: like listens to like
decisions.reason: People show who they are by what they like to hear.

records.source: לֹעֵ֣ג לָ֭רָשׁ חֵרֵ֣ף עֹשֵׂ֑הוּ שָׂמֵ֥חַ לְ֝אֵ֗יד לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶֽה׃
records.gloss: [One] mocking [the] poor insults his Maker; [one] glad at calamity will not go unpunished.
pieces: Whoever mocks the poor insults the One who made them; \q whoever gloats over disaster will not escape punishment.

L.5: Whoever mocks [the] poor insults {{gender:their|his}} Maker; \q whoever is glad at disaster will not go unpunished.

R.5: If you make fun of poor people, you insult God, who made them. \q If you are happy when bad things happen to others, you will be punished.

decisions.choice: insults his Maker: as in 14:31

records.source: עֲטֶ֣רֶת זְ֭קֵנִים בְּנֵ֣י בָנִ֑ים וְתִפְאֶ֖רֶת בָּנִ֣ים אֲבוֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: [The] crown of old [people] [is] children of children, and [the] glory of children [is] their fathers.
pieces: Grandchildren are the crown of the elderly, \q and children take pride in their {{gender:parents|fathers}}.

L.6: Grandchildren [are the] crown of [the] old, \q and [the] glory of children [is] their {{gender:parents|fathers}}.

R.6: Grandparents are proud of their grandchildren. \q Children are proud of their parents.

decisions.choice: fathers: parents, forebears
decisions.reason: The word (abot) can mean ancestors or parents in general.

records.source: לֹא־נָאוָ֣ה לְנָבָ֣ל שְׂפַת־יֶ֑תֶר אַ֝֗ף כִּֽי־לְנָדִ֥יב שְׂפַת־שָֽׁקֶר׃
records.gloss: Not fitting for a fool [is] a lip of excellence; how much less for a noble a lip of falsehood!
pieces: Eloquent words do not suit a fool; \q still less do lies suit a leader.

L.7: Fine speech is not fitting for a fool; \q how much less lying lips for a noble!

R.7: It is strange to hear a fool speak well. \q It is even worse to hear a leader tell lies.

decisions.choice: fool: the nabal, the boorish fool
decisions.reason: This word for fool (nabal) is the name of the man in 1 Samuel 25:25: crude, godless and closed to reason.

records.source: אֶֽבֶן־חֵ֣ן הַ֭שֹּׁחַד בְּעֵינֵ֣י בְעָלָ֑יו אֶֽל־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֖ר יִפְנֶ֣ה יַשְׂכִּֽיל׃
records.gloss: A stone of favor [is] the bribe in [the] eyes of its owner; to all that he turns he prospers.
pieces: A bribe seems like a lucky charm to the one who gives it; \q wherever he turns, it works.

L.8: A bribe [is] a stone of favor in [the] eyes of its owner; \q wherever it turns, it succeeds.

R.8: People who give bribes think bribes are like magic. \q They think a bribe can get them anything.

decisions.choice: a stone of favor: a charm, in the giver's eyes
decisions.reason: The saying describes how bribers see things, not how God sees them; verse 23 condemns the bribe.

records.source: מְֽכַסֶּה־פֶּ֭שַׁע מְבַקֵּ֣שׁ אַהֲבָ֑ה וְשֹׁנֶ֥ה בְ֝דָבָ֗ר מַפְרִ֥יד אַלּֽוּף׃
records.gloss: [One] covering a transgression seeks love, but [one] repeating a matter separates a close friend.
pieces: Whoever forgives a wrong builds up love, \q but whoever keeps bringing it up drives friends apart.

L.9: Whoever covers an offense seeks love, \q but whoever repeats a matter separates close friends.

R.9: If you forgive people, you help them love you. \q If you keep talking about what they did wrong, you lose friends.

decisions.choice: covers an offense: as in 10:12

records.source: תֵּ֣חַת גְּעָרָ֣ה בְמֵבִ֑ין מֵהַכּ֖וֹת כְּסִ֣יל מֵאָֽה׃
records.gloss: A rebuke goes deeper in [one] understanding than striking a fool a hundred [times].
pieces: A single rebuke does more for a person of understanding \q than a hundred lashes for a fool.

L.10: A rebuke goes deeper into one who understands \q than a hundred blows into a fool.

R.10: A wise person learns more from one warning \q than a fool learns from being beaten a hundred times.

decisions.choice: a hundred blows: far more than the law allowed
decisions.reason: The law limited a beating to forty strokes (Deuteronomy 25:3). The number is for effect.

records.source: אַךְ־מְרִ֥י יְבַקֶּשׁ־רָ֑ע וּמַלְאָ֥ךְ אַ֝כְזָרִ֗י יְשֻׁלַּח־בּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Only rebellion an evil [person] seeks, and a cruel messenger will be sent against him.
pieces: The wicked are bent only on rebellion, \q so a merciless messenger will be sent against them.

L.11: An evil person seeks only rebellion, \q and a cruel messenger will be sent against {{gender:them|him}}.

R.11: Evil people only want to rebel. \q So someone cruel will be sent to punish them.

decisions.choice: a cruel messenger: an officer of punishment, or an angel of judgment
decisions.reason: The messenger (malak) may be a king's officer or an angel sent in judgment (Psalm 78:49).

records.source: פָּג֬וֹשׁ דֹּ֣ב שַׁכּ֣וּל בְּאִ֑ישׁ וְאַל־כְּ֝סִ֗יל בְּאִוַּלְתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Let a bear robbed of cubs meet a person, and not a fool in his folly.
pieces: Facing a mother bear robbed of her cubs is safer \q than facing a fool in the middle of his folly.

L.12: Better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs \q than a fool in {{gender:their|his}} folly.

R.12: It is better to meet an angry mother bear whose cubs were taken \q than a fool doing something foolish.

decisions.choice: a bear robbed of her cubs: the most dangerous animal
decisions.reason: Bears lived in Israel then (2 Kings 2:24; Hosea 13:8).

records.source: מֵשִׁ֣יב רָ֭עָה תַּ֣חַת טוֹבָ֑ה לֹא־תָמ֥וּשׁ רָ֝עָ֗ה מִבֵּיתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: [One] returning evil for good, evil will not depart from his house.
pieces: If anyone pays back good with evil, \q evil will never leave their house.

L.13: Whoever repays evil for good, \q evil will not leave {{gender:their|his}} house.

R.13: If you do evil to people who are good to you, \q evil will always be in your home.

decisions.choice: evil for good: as with David and Nabal
decisions.reason: David said Nabal had "repaid me evil for good" (1 Samuel 25:21); compare Psalm 35:12.

decisions.choice: will depart, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The ketiv and qere spell this verb differently; the meaning is the same.

records.source: פּ֣וֹטֵֽר מַ֭יִם רֵאשִׁ֣ית מָד֑וֹן וְלִפְנֵ֥י הִ֝תְגַּלַּ֗ע הָרִ֥יב נְטֽוֹשׁ׃
records.gloss: [One] letting out water [is the] beginning of strife, and before the quarrel breaks out, abandon [it].
pieces: Starting a quarrel is like breaching a dam; \q so drop it before the fight bursts out.

L.14: Starting a quarrel [is like] letting out water; \q so drop [the matter] before the dispute breaks out.

R.14: Starting an argument is like making a hole in a dam: it is hard to stop. \q So stop before a fight starts.

decisions.choice: letting out water: a small leak that becomes a flood
decisions.reason: Once water breaks through it cannot be called back.

records.source: מַצְדִּ֣יק רָ֭שָׁע וּמַרְשִׁ֣יעַ צַדִּ֑יק תּוֹעֲבַ֥ת יְ֝הוָ֗ה גַּם־שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: [One] justifying [the] wicked and [one] condemning [the] righteous, an abomination of YHWH [are] even both of them.
pieces: Acquitting the guilty and condemning the innocent: \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} detests them both.

L.15: Whoever acquits [the] wicked and whoever condemns [the] righteous, \q both alike [are] an abomination to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.15: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} hates it when judges let guilty people go free. \q He also hates it when they punish innocent people.

decisions.choice: acquits ... condemns: judges in court
decisions.reason: The verbs are legal terms (Deuteronomy 25:1; Isaiah 5:23).

records.source: לָמָּה־זֶּ֣ה מְחִ֣יר בְּיַד־כְּסִ֑יל לִקְנ֖וֹת חָכְמָ֣ה וְלֶב־אָֽיִן׃
records.gloss: Why this, a price in [the] hand of a fool to acquire wisdom, and heart there is not?
pieces: What use is money in a fool's hand to buy wisdom, \q when he has no mind to learn?

L.16: Why [is there] money in a fool's hand to buy wisdom, \q when [he has] no heart [for it]?

R.16: A fool may have money to pay for teaching. \q But it is useless, because he does not want to learn.

decisions.choice: a price to buy wisdom: paying a teacher
decisions.reason: Wisdom must be acquired (4:5, 7), but money cannot buy it without the will to learn.

records.source: בְּכָל־עֵ֭ת אֹהֵ֣ב הָרֵ֑עַ וְאָ֥ח לְ֝צָרָ֗ה יִוָּלֵֽד׃
records.gloss: At every time the friend loves, and a brother is born for adversity.
pieces: A friend is loving through every season, \q and a brother is born to stand with you in trouble.

L.17: A friend loves at all times, \q and a brother is born for adversity.

R.17: A true friend always loves you. \q A brother is there to help you when life is hard.

decisions.choice: friend ... brother: two kinds of loyalty
alternatives: the friend is a brother in adversity
decisions.reason: The lines may contrast the two or describe one person: a real friend becomes a brother in trouble (18:24).

decisions.choice: brother, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The saying names a brother as kin; the word is kept, since the point is family loyalty.

records.source: אָדָ֣ם חֲסַר־לֵ֭ב תּוֹקֵ֣עַ כָּ֑ף עֹרֵ֥ב עֲ֝רֻבָּ֗ה לִפְנֵ֥י רֵעֵֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: A person lacking heart strikes a palm, pledging a pledge before his neighbor.
pieces: Only someone with no sense shakes hands on a pledge \q and puts up security for a neighbor.

L.18: A person lacking heart strikes hands [in pledge], \q becoming surety before {{gender:their|his}} neighbor.

R.18: It is foolish to promise to pay someone else's debts.

decisions.choice: strikes hands, becomes surety: as in 6:1–5
decisions.reason: See 6:1.

records.source: אֹ֣הֵֽב פֶּ֭שַׁע אֹהֵ֣ב מַצָּ֑ה מַגְבִּ֥יהַּ פִּ֝תְח֗וֹ מְבַקֶּשׁ־שָֽׁבֶר׃
records.gloss: [One] loving transgression loves strife; [one] making high his doorway seeks destruction.
pieces: Whoever loves quarrels loves sin; \q whoever builds a high gate invites ruin.

L.19: Whoever loves offense loves strife; \q whoever makes {{gender:their|his}} door high seeks destruction.

R.19: People who like to argue like to do wrong. \q People who show off are asking for trouble.

decisions.choice: makes his door high: shows off, or boasts
alternatives: talks big (his mouth as a door)
decisions.reason: A high gate is a show of wealth and pride; or "his door" means his mouth (Micah 7:5), talking proudly.

records.source: עִקֶּשׁ־לֵ֭ב לֹ֣א יִמְצָא־ט֑וֹב וְנֶהְפָּ֥ךְ בִּ֝לְשׁוֹנ֗וֹ יִפּ֥וֹל בְּרָעָֽה׃
records.gloss: [One] perverse of heart does not find good, and [one] twisted in his tongue falls into trouble.
pieces: A crooked heart finds nothing good, \q and a deceitful tongue lands in trouble.

L.20: [One] crooked of heart does not find good, \q and one twisted in {{gender:their|his}} tongue falls into trouble.

R.20: People with evil thoughts will not find anything good. \q People who lie will get into trouble.

decisions.choice: twisted: turned over
decisions.reason: The root of "perverse things" in 2:12.

records.source: יֹלֵ֣ד כְּ֭סִיל לְת֣וּגָה ל֑וֹ וְלֹֽא־יִ֝שְׂמַ֗ח אֲבִ֣י נָבָֽל׃
records.gloss: [One] fathering a fool [does so] to his grief, and the father of a fool does not rejoice.
pieces: To raise a fool is to grieve; \q the father of a fool knows no joy.

L.21: Whoever fathers a fool [has] grief, \q and the father of a fool has no joy.

R.21: It is sad to have a son who is a fool. \q His father will not be happy.

decisions.choice: fool ... fool: two words (kesil, nabal)
decisions.reason: Two words for fool; see 17:7.

records.source: לֵ֣ב שָׂ֭מֵחַ יֵיטִ֣ב גֵּהָ֑ה וְר֥וּחַ נְ֝כֵאָ֗ה תְּיַבֶּשׁ־גָּֽרֶם׃
records.gloss: A glad heart does good [as] healing, but a stricken spirit dries up bone.
pieces: A cheerful heart heals like medicine, \q but a broken spirit saps the body's strength.

L.22: A cheerful heart does good [like] medicine, \q but a crushed spirit dries up [the] bones.

R.22: Being happy is good for your health. \q Being sad can make you feel weak.

decisions.choice: medicine: healing
decisions.reason: The word (gehah) is found only here.

records.source: שֹׁ֣חַד מֵ֭חֵיק רָשָׁ֣ע יִקָּ֑ח לְ֝הַטּ֗וֹת אָרְח֥וֹת מִשְׁפָּֽט׃
records.gloss: A bribe from [the] bosom a wicked [person] takes, to turn aside [the] paths of justice.
pieces: The wicked accept a bribe slipped from a pocket \q to twist the course of justice.

L.23: [The] wicked takes a bribe from [the] bosom \q to pervert [the] ways of justice.

R.23: Evil judges take secret bribes so they can be unfair in court.

decisions.choice: from the bosom: secretly
decisions.reason: The fold of the garment at the chest served as a pocket (21:14).

records.source: אֶת־פְּנֵ֣י מֵבִ֣ין חָכְמָ֑ה וְעֵינֵ֥י כְ֝סִ֗יל בִּקְצֵה־אָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: With [the] face of [one] understanding [is] wisdom, but [the] eyes of a fool [are] at [the] end of [the] earth.
pieces: The discerning keep wisdom in view, \q but a fool's eyes wander to the ends of the earth.

L.24: Wisdom [is] before [the] face of [one who] understands, \q but [the] eyes of a fool [are] at [the] ends of [the] earth.

R.24: Wise people keep their minds on being wise. \q Fools let their minds wander everywhere.

decisions.choice: eyes at the ends of the earth: wandering, unfocused
decisions.reason: Wisdom is near at hand; the fool looks everywhere else (Deuteronomy 30:11–14).

records.source: כַּ֣עַס לְ֭אָבִיו בֵּ֣ן כְּסִ֑יל וּ֝מֶ֗מֶר לְיוֹלַדְתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Grief to his father [is] a foolish son, and bitterness to her who bore him.
pieces: A son who is a fool is a sorrow to his father \q and a bitter grief to the mother who bore him.

L.25: A foolish son [is] grief to his father \q and bitterness to her who bore him.

R.25: A foolish son makes his father sad \q and his mother sad too.

decisions.choice: a foolish son: as in 10:1 and 17:21

records.source: גַּ֤ם עֲנ֣וֹשׁ לַצַּדִּ֣יק לֹא־ט֑וֹב לְהַכּ֖וֹת נְדִיבִ֣ים עַל־יֹֽשֶׁר׃
records.gloss: Also to fine the righteous [is] not good, to strike nobles for uprightness.
pieces: It is wrong to fine the innocent, \q or to flog officials for their honesty.

L.26: To fine the righteous [is] not good, \q [nor] to flog nobles for [their] uprightness.

R.26: It is wrong to punish innocent people. \q It is wrong to beat good leaders for being honest.

decisions.choice: nobles: officials, people of standing
decisions.reason: The word (nedibim) of 8:16.

records.source: חוֹשֵׂ֣ךְ אֲ֭מָרָיו יוֹדֵ֣עַ דָּ֑עַת יְקַר־ר֝֗וּחַ אִ֣ישׁ תְּבוּנָֽה׃
records.gloss: [One] restraining his words knows knowledge, and noble of spirit [is] a person of understanding.
pieces: Whoever holds back words has knowledge, \q and someone with a steady spirit has understanding.

L.27: Whoever restrains {{gender:their|his}} words knows knowledge, \q and [one] noble of spirit [is] a person of understanding.

R.27: People who know a lot do not talk too much. \q People who understand keep control of themselves.

decisions.choice: noble (precious) of spirit, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) read "cool of spirit", calm; the reading the scribes marked (qere) is "precious of spirit". Both describe self-control.

records.source: גַּ֤ם אֱוִ֣יל מַ֭חֲרִישׁ חָכָ֣ם יֵחָשֵׁ֑ב אֹטֵ֖ם שְׂפָתָ֣יו נָבֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: Even a fool keeping silent is considered wise; [one] shutting his lips, discerning.
pieces: Even fools are thought wise if they keep quiet; \q if they close their lips, they seem discerning.

L.28: Even a fool who keeps silent is counted wise; \q one who shuts {{gender:their|his}} lips, discerning.

R.28: Even foolish people seem wise when they keep quiet. \q If they do not say anything, people think they are smart.

decisions.choice: is counted wise: seems so to others
decisions.reason: A wry observation, following verse 27.
